```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# The examples need Java and the JDemetra+ v3 packages
can_run <- requireNamespace("rjd3x13", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("rjd3tramoseats", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("rjd3toolkit", quietly = TRUE) &&
    isTRUE(rjd3jars::check_java_version(silent = TRUE))
has_plot <- can_run &&
    requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("ggtime", quietly = TRUE)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = can_run)
```

## Introduction

`fable.rjd3` lets you seasonally adjust `tsibble` series with the JDemetra+ v3
algorithms, using the [`fabletools`](https://fabletools.tidyverts.org/)
modelling framework. Four models are available:

| Model | Algorithm | Decomposition |
|:------|:----------|:--------------|
| `X13()` | X-13ARIMA (`rjd3x13::jx13()`) | yes |
| `TRAMOSEATS()` | TRAMO-SEATS (`rjd3tramoseats::jtramoseats()`) | yes |
| `REGARIMA()` | Reg-ARIMA pre-adjustment only (`rjd3x13::jregarima()`) | no |
| `TRAMO()` | TRAMO pre-adjustment only (`rjd3tramoseats::jtramo()`) | no |

The fitted models keep the underlying **Java object**. The usual decomposition
is available through `components()`, and *any* other JDemetra+ indicator
(outliers, regression coefficients, diagnostics...) can be extracted with
`jd3_indicator()`.

The package re-exports the main verbs of `fabletools` (`model()`,
`components()`, `forecast()`, `glance()`, `tidy()`, `report()`...) and a few
functions of `tsibble`, so that `library(fable.rjd3)` is enough.

```{r load}
library(fable.rjd3)
```

## Quick start

The series must be a univariate `tsibble` with a `yearmonth` or `yearquarter`
index and no gaps. The frequency is deduced from the interval between the
observations, so monthly, bimonthly, quarterly, four-monthly and semi-annual
series are all supported (for example, a `yearmonth` index with a step of 2
months is a bimonthly series, with a step of 6 months a semi-annual one). Here we
use the classic `AirPassengers` data.

```{r data}
air <- as_tsibble(AirPassengers)
air
```

Models are fitted with `model()`, exactly as with other `fable` models. Several
models can be fitted at once, which makes it easy to compare the two methods.

```{r fit}
mb <- model(
    air,
    x13 = X13(value),
    ts  = TRAMOSEATS(value)
)
mb
```

The model summary shows the method and the selected ARIMA model.

## Decomposition

For `X13()` and `TRAMOSEATS()`, `components()` returns a `dable` with the
original series and the columns `trend`, `seasonal`, `irregular` and
`season_adjust`. The relation between the components follows the decomposition
mode of the model (additive, multiplicative, log-additive or pseudo-additive).

```{r components}
components(mb)
```

With the `ggtime` package, the decomposition can be plotted with `autoplot()`.

```{r autoplot, eval = has_plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
library(ggtime)
ggplot2::autoplot(components(mb))
```

## Setting the specification

The specification can be defined in two ways, which can be combined.

### Ex ante, with the `spec` argument

`spec` accepts a name (such as `"rsa3"` for `X13()` or `"rsafull"` for
`TRAMOSEATS()`), or a specification object created with `rjd3x13::x13_spec()` /
`rjd3tramoseats::tramoseats_spec()` and modified with the `set_*()` functions
of `rjd3toolkit`. This gives access to everything JDemetra+ offers.

```{r spec-exante}
my_spec <- rjd3x13::x13_spec("rsa3")
my_spec <- rjd3toolkit::set_transform(my_spec, fun = "Log")
my_spec <- rjd3toolkit::add_outlier(my_spec, type = "AO", date = "1955-01-01")

mb_spec <- model(air, x13 = X13(value, spec = my_spec))
glance(mb_spec)
```

### In the formula, with specials

Specials are used on the right-hand side of the formula. Each one records a call
to a function of `rjd3toolkit` (or of the algorithm package) that is applied to
the base specification:

| Special | Calls |
|:--------|:------|
| `spec(x)` | base specification, same as the `spec` argument |
| `basic(...)` | `rjd3toolkit::set_basic()` |
| `transform(...)` | `rjd3toolkit::set_transform()` |
| `estimate(...)` | `rjd3toolkit::set_estimate()` |
| `automodel(...)` | `rjd3toolkit::set_automodel()` |
| `outlier(...)` | `rjd3toolkit::set_outlier()` |
| `add_outlier(...)` | `rjd3toolkit::add_outlier()` |
| `easter(...)` | `rjd3toolkit::set_easter()` |
| `tradingdays(...)` | `rjd3toolkit::set_tradingdays()` |
| `arima(...)` | `rjd3toolkit::set_arima()` |
| `ramp(...)` | `rjd3toolkit::add_ramp()` |
| `usrdefvar(...)` | `rjd3toolkit::add_usrdefvar()` |
| `benchmarking(...)` | `rjd3toolkit::set_benchmarking()` (`X13()` and `TRAMOSEATS()`) |
| `x11(...)` | `rjd3x13::set_x11()` (`X13()` only) |
| `seats(...)` | `rjd3tramoseats::set_seats()` (`TRAMOSEATS()` only) |
| `xreg(...)` | user regressors taken from tsibble columns |

```{r specials}
mb_sp <- model(
    air,
    x13 = X13(
        value ~ transform(fun = "Log") +
            outlier(outliers.type = c("AO", "LS")) +
            x11(seasonal.filter = "S3X5")
    )
)
glance(mb_sp)
```

The base `spec` is applied first, then the specials in a fixed order, then
`xreg()`: later settings override earlier ones. A special that does not apply to
the method (for example `x11()` in `TRAMOSEATS()`) is ignored with a warning.

The base specification is also stored in the model as the *reference
specification* (argument `ref_spec`, by default equal to `spec`). It is the
reference used by the refresh policies of `refit()` and `stream()`, see below.

### Regressors from the tsibble

Since a specification created ex ante cannot refer to columns of your data,
regressors are declared with the `xreg()` special. The variables are added to
the modelling context, and to the specification when `regeffect` is given.

```{r xreg}
air$shock <- as.numeric(air$index == yearmonth("1955 Jan"))

mb_xreg <- model(air, x13 = X13(value ~ xreg(shock, regeffect = "Series")))
tidy(mb_xreg)
```

For custom calendars, build a context with `rjd3toolkit::modelling_context()`
and pass it through the `context` argument.

## Extracting results

### Diagnostics and regression terms

* `glance()` returns a one-row summary per model: information criteria,
  number of observations and outliers, tests on the residuals and, for seasonal
  adjustment models, tests on the seasonally adjusted series and the quality
  statistics of the method. Tests give two columns (`_stat` and `_pvalue`) and
  the combined seasonality tests give a text. The set of indicators depends on
  the method; `glance(x, ids = )` takes a vector of indicator ids to choose
  others.
* `tidy()` returns one row per coefficient (ARIMA parameters, regression
  variables, outliers, calendar effects) with its standard error, statistic and
  p-value. Coefficients fixed in the specification are included.
* `report()` prints a summary of one model: the coefficients and the tests, in
  the spirit of `summary()` for a regression.

```{r glance}
glance(mb)
tidy(mb_sp)
report(mb["x13"])
```

### Outliers

`outliers()` returns the rows of the data identified as outliers (additive
outliers, level shifts, transitory changes, seasonal outliers) by the
pre-adjustment model. The `type` argument keeps some types only, and the type
and the statistics of each outlier are available in `tidy()`.

```{r outliers}
outliers(mb)
outliers(mb, type = "AO")
```

### Any JDemetra+ indicator

`jd3_dictionary()` lists the indicators available for a model, and
`jd3_indicator()` extracts one of them via `rjd3toolkit::result()`.

```{r indicators}
head(jd3_dictionary(mb), 15)

# the raw object, for a single model
jd3_indicator(mb$x13[[1]], "sa")

# the same indicator for all the models of the mable
jd3_indicator(mb, "sa")
```

For a mable, the result depends on the type of the indicator: a number gives a
column `value`, a series is returned in long format (`index` and `value`), and a
test gives the columns `statistic`, `p.value` and `distribution`. With several
ids, a named list is returned.

```{r indicators-several}
jd3_indicator(mb, "residuals.lb")
jd3_indicator(mb, c("likelihood.aicc", "likelihood.nobs"))
```

## Pre-adjustment models and forecasts

`REGARIMA()` and `TRAMO()` fit the pre-adjustment model only, with the same
specifications and specials as `X13()` and `TRAMOSEATS()`. They have no
decomposition, so no `components()`, but all the other methods work.

```{r regarima}
mb_pre <- model(air, regarima = REGARIMA(value), tramo = TRAMO(value))
glance(mb_pre)
```

### Forecasts and backcasts

`forecast()` forecasts the raw series from the pre-adjustment model, for the four
models. The result is a distribution: log-normal if the series is
log-transformed, normal otherwise. The default point forecast `.mean` is the mean
of the distribution; use `point_forecast` to choose another summary, for example
the median, which is the forecast given by JDemetra+.

```{r forecast}
forecast(mb_pre, h = 12)
forecast(mb_pre, h = 12, point_forecast = list(.median = median))
```

`backcast()` does the same for the periods preceding the series.

```{r backcast}
backcast(mb, h = 12)
```

### Fitted values, residuals and missing values

`fitted()` and `residuals()` give the one-step-ahead fitted values and the
residuals of the pre-adjustment model, with `NA` where they are not defined. They
make `augment()` and `accuracy()` work.

```{r fitted}
residuals(mb)
augment(mb)
```

`interpolate()` replaces the missing values of the series by the estimates of the
model.

```{r interpolate}
air_na <- air
air_na$value[c(20, 21)] <- NA
mb_na <- model(air_na, x13 = X13(value))
interpolate(mb_na, air_na)
```

## Updating models

When new observations arrive, a model can be updated with the refresh policies of
JDemetra+ (`"Fixed"` by default: the estimated parameters are kept; the other
policies are `"FreeParameters"`, `"Complete"`, `"Outliers_StochasticComponent"`,
`"Outliers"`, `"FixedParameters"`, `"FixedAutoRegressiveParameters"` and
`"Current"`). The refresh is based on the estimated specification and on the
reference specification stored in the model.

* `stream()` appends the new observations to the data of the model;
* `refit()` applies the model to a new complete dataset.

```{r update}
start_new <- yearmonth("1960 Jan")
air_old <- air[air$index < start_new, c("index", "value")]
air_new <- air[air$index >= start_new, c("index", "value")]
mb_old  <- model(air_old, x13 = X13(value))

mb_ext <- stream(mb_old, air_new)
components(mb_ext)

mb_refit <- refit(mb_old, air[c("index", "value")], policy = "FreeParameters")
```

## Several series

Because models are defined through `fabletools`, keyed tsibbles work as usual:
one model is fitted per series.

```{r keys}
a <- as.data.frame(air[c("index", "value")]); a$series <- "A"
b <- a; b$value <- sqrt(b$value) * 10; b$series <- "B"
two <- as_tsibble(rbind(a, b), index = index, key = series)

mb2 <- model(two, x13 = X13(value))
mb2
glance(mb2)
```

## JDemetra+ workspaces

`import_jws()` reads a JDemetra+ workspace and fits its SA-items with the
specifications it contains. The result is a mable with two keys, `sap` (the
SA-processing) and `series` (the SA-item), and a model column `sa`. The
estimation specification of the item is the specification of the model, its
reference specification is kept for the refresh policies, and the modelling
context of the workspace (calendars and user-defined variables) is shared by all
the models.

```{r workspace}
file <- system.file("workspaces", "workspace_test.xml", package = "rjd3workspace")
mb_jws <- import_jws(file)
mb_jws
```

`export_jws()` does the opposite: it writes a new workspace, readable by the
JDemetra+ graphical interface, from a mable of models. A workspace has a single
context, so regressors of different series that have the same name but different
values are renamed `<name>_<sap>_<series>`, in the context and in the
specifications. Results, comments and links to data providers are not exported,
and the series are stored as static data.

```{r export}
export_jws(mb_jws, tempfile(fileext = ".xml"))
```

## Saving and reloading models

The Java object cannot be serialized: after `saveRDS()` / `readRDS()` (or when a
model is created on a `future` worker) the Java pointer is no longer valid.
`fable.rjd3` handles this transparently: the data, the specifications and the
context are stored as regular R objects, and the first time an extraction
(`components()`, `glance()`, `jd3_indicator()`, `forecast()`...) is called on a
reloaded model, the model is re-estimated. The following calls use the new Java
object.

```{r saving}
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(mb, f)
mb_reloaded <- readRDS(f)

components(mb_reloaded)                 # the models are re-estimated here
jd3_indicator(mb_reloaded, "sa")        # no new estimation
```

The estimation uses the versions of the `rjd3*` packages installed when the
model is reloaded, which can differ from the versions used to fit it.

## Limitations

* Only `yearmonth` and `yearquarter` indices are supported, and the series
  must be univariate and regular. The interval between observations must divide
  a year, and a series with an interval of several months must start at the
  beginning of a period (for example in January or July for a semi-annual series).
* The forecasts are those of the pre-adjustment model of the raw series; the
  components (trend, seasonal, irregular) are not forecasted.
* The available indicator ids depend on the installed version of the
  `rjd3*` packages; use `jd3_dictionary()` to list them.
* `import_jws()` only imports the SA-items estimated with an X-13ARIMA or a
  TRAMO-SEATS specification.
